propositions: Context-limit escalation on a provider-qualified run (e.g., Bedrock) silently relocates the call to a bare Anthropic model id, discarding the provider qualifier and causing hard failures or unbudgeted spend.

The _rung_target function derives both sides of its provider comparison from the ladder constant, never considering the run's actual model, so the rung degrades to a bare Anthropic family name whenever the class table has not been retargeted.

With no model-class table configured and a Bedrock-qualified primary, the one-criterion retry receives a bare model id instead of the provider-qualified original, and higher rungs incorrectly escalate to Anthropic family names.

The fix threads the primary model into _rung_target and compares inferred providers: if they agree or either is undeterminable, return today's value; if they differ on the primary's own rung, return the primary verbatim; if they differ on a higher rung, drop the rung and stop escalation.
